entries.summary: Bearish elevated downside-risk bias retained, with lower conviction following Thursday's intraday reversal. Reuters reports Nasdaq +0.31%, SOX +0.2%, NVDA approximately -4%, AMD +7%, AVGO +5.4% after Nasdaq opened -1.47% and NVDA had earlier fallen more than 12%. The 10Y Treasury yield reached 5.066%, up 7.73bp. These readings are asynchronous, not a synchronized quote set. QQQ, VXN/VIX, breadth, live 2Y and curve remain unavailable. Open Watch remains 159 events. Friday PPI is the next major macro catalyst.
bullish: Nasdaq +0.31% and SOX +0.2% in Reuters intraday reporting show recovery from opening losses.
AMD +7% and AVGO +5.4% indicate chip-sector rotation rather than indiscriminate liquidation.
Foxconn and Siemens AI infrastructure demand support longer-run fundamentals, without an attributable intraday market reaction.
bearish: Nvidia remains approximately 4% lower amid leadership and export-policy uncertainty.
10Y Treasury yield at 5.066%, up 7.73 basis points, raises discount-rate pressure.
Friday October PPI could amplify rate and equity volatility; closing breadth is unconfirmed.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq and semiconductors have reversed Thursday's initial selloff even while Nvidia remains lower. Reuters reports Nasdaq Composite +0.31% and SOX +0.2%, NVDA about -4%, AMD +7% and Broadcom +5.4%. The evidence suggests sector rotation rather than indiscriminate selling, although higher Treasury yields and the unresolved Nvidia succession keep the three-day downside scenario elevated.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the previous 10:30 EST assessment, Reuters has reported Nasdaq and SOX turning positive after the opening selloff, while Nvidia recovered substantially from its early losses. The 10Y yield reached 5.066%, up 7.73bp. The curated Open Watch feed remains 159 events. The intraday recovery reduces confidence in a cascading selloff but does not yet constitute a durable multi-session directional reversal.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The observed market response differs from the initial expected catalyst impact. Nvidia's confirmed CEO transition has caused company-specific weakness, but AMD and AVGO gains offset some sector pressure. The Reuters numbers have unspecified individual quote times and cannot establish synchronized breadth or SOX-versus-QQQ strength. A live 2Y yield is missing, so no current 10Y–2Y spread can be calculated. Historical 4.988% minus 4.731% equals +25.7 basis points, not hundreds of percent.
editorial.threeDayPath: Thursday November 12's closing breadth and semiconductor relative strength will determine whether the recovery is sustainable. Friday November 13's 08:30 EST October PPI may intensify rate-sensitive selling or allow relief to extend. Monday November 16 tests whether leadership uncertainty spreads across AI infrastructure or remains concentrated in Nvidia. The bearish bias remains conditional, not a forecast of specific index returns.
editorial.bullCase: An orderly Nvidia transition, persistent AMD and Broadcom strength, and resilient AI infrastructure orders could support a broad recovery. A positive Nasdaq/SOX close, stronger breadth and contained VXN/VIX and Treasury yields would undermine the bearish scenario.
editorial.bearCase: A failed intraday recovery, adverse Nvidia governance or export-control news, and a hotter-than-expected PPI could restart broad technology selling. The 10Y yield above 5% remains a significant valuation headwind and a further rise would threaten growth leadership.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the closing QQQ, Nasdaq and SOX moves, SOX-versus-QQQ relative strength, market breadth, VXN/VIX, matched 10Y and 2Y yields, fresh oil and FedWatch, and Nvidia/AMD/AVGO follow-through. Check Cisco and Applied Materials after-close earnings, Friday PPI at 08:30 EST, and Monday continuation.
